Contract.title: One canonical skill copy in the source tree, with distribution materialized at build time
Contract.Problem: Intervention I-015 records P-021: each of four lifecycle skills exists four times, as `skills/`, `packages/skills/`, `packages/claude-plugin/skills/` and `packages/openpackage/skills/`, so sixteen tracked `SKILL.md` bodies stand for four skills. The generator already establishes one authoring source, but the mirrored bodies are tracked ordinary source and drift.
Contract.Change: `skills/` remains the sole maintained source-tree skill content. The three distribution layouts are generated deterministically at build or release staging rather than tracked as ordinary source, and `.gitignore` excludes the generated trees. Format-specific manifests and generation logic remain. The CLI skill refresh resolves canonical content in a source checkout and the explicitly packaged resource in an installed distribution; it does not depend on a removed generated directory or an incidental prior build. Package verification detects stale, missing or extra distribution content without requiring tracked source bodies. Direct repository consumers receive a verified compatible route or an explicit compatibility decision. Historical upgrade tests, examples, package checks and the local `grace5-release` skill still pass.

Constraints.Constraint: No skill-semantic rewrite, release, version bump, migration boundary or client rollout; the same skill bytes are generated and compared before and after the layout change.
Installed skill refresh remains a kernel-managed write; the change adds no project-file write and no new migration boundary.
`skills/` is source, generated packages are build artifacts, and installed `grace5-*` directories remain kernel-managed and excluded from the candidate.
One ledger entry records build-time package materialization and its removal criterion; L-26 is amended to name the remaining skill source it guards.
No symlink-dependent layout: Windows, archive and installer behaviour is proven before adoption.
No packaging abstraction beyond build-time materialization and no replacement of full installable skill content with references that resolve only in the framework checkout.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No change to the skill text or lifecycle semantics; generated bytes are compared before and after the layout change.
No release, tag, version, pin or migration-table change.
No automatic client rollout and no historical upgrade rewrite.
No new package format or consumer without an explicit compatibility decision.

Acceptance.Criterion: A fresh source checkout has one canonical copy per lifecycle skill and runs the required checks without manually manufacturing missing package directories.
The three distribution artifacts are generated deterministically, contain the required skill content and resources, and install independently of the source checkout.
Source-checkout and installed-package upgrade paths refresh the correct bytes; repeated upgrade is idempotent and project-owned skills remain untouched.
Package verification detects stale, missing or extra distribution content without redundant tracked bodies; a direct repository consumer has a verified route or an explicit compatibility decision.
Historical upgrade tests, examples and package checks pass; the local release skill is preserved; any packaged watchdog import resolves after installation.
No version, pin, tag or migration row moves.
The package generator, skill resolver and upgrade code type-check with the rest of the kernel.

Decisions.Decision: `skills/` is the sole maintained source; distribution layouts are materialized at build or release staging and are not tracked ordinary source.
Generated packages are ignored in the source tree; `.gitignore` states it, and a fresh checkout runs the checks without a prior build.
Package verification needs no tracked package bodies: it regenerates deterministically and detects stale, missing or extra distribution content.

The CLI refresh resolves canonical content in a source checkout and the explicitly packaged resource in an installed distribution; it never depends on an incidental prior build or a removed directory.
Every direct consumer of `packages/` is inventoried; a consumer either has a verified compatible route or is named in the compatibility decision.
Symlinks are not assumed to work on Windows, in archives or in installers; the layout is proven with real files.
This change coordinates with the package-owned installation rule and the packaged advisor resource so neither introduces a second source or a duplicate watchdog.
No release, version, pin, tag or migration row is part of this change; the release act remains separate and owner-requested.
The local `grace5-release` skill is preserved and is not packaged as a shipped skill.
